blocks.text: The module documentation specifies handshake negotiation, credential separation, frame limits, validation, close codes, handler behavior, logging restrictions, and lazy runtime requirements.
blocks.title: Protocol and security contract

blocks.anchor: REVALIDATE_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 30.0      # the rule: at most 30; SETTINGS makes it injectable
blocks.text: SocketSettings centralizes injectable timeouts and limits. ProtocolUnavailable, candidate paths, a lock, and caches support lazy validator loading.
blocks.title: Settings and protocol state

blocks.text: load_protocol searches backend and repository protocol directories under a lock, imports validate.py once, and converts load failures into a fixed ProtocolUnavailable error. Cache reset and client-type extraction support tests and negotiation.
blocks.title: Lazy schema loading

blocks.text: MessageHandler defines the post-handshake callback contract, UnavailableHandler returns a fixed error until a run manager is installed, and _ref_id extracts safe UUID references.
blocks.title: Handler seam and frame identity

blocks.text: Frames are classified as disconnect, oversized, binary, or text. JSON parsing and tolerant protocol validation produce fixed errors, while _reject sends one error followed by a close frame before authentication.
blocks.title: Frame parsing and rejection

blocks.text: The handshake enforces timing, size, binary, first-message, and protocol-version rules, records selected failures, and authenticates the device credential in a worker thread.
blocks.title: Hello authentication

blocks.anchor: async def _read_loop(conn: DeviceConnection, websocket, protocol, settings, handler) -> None:
blocks.text: The receive loop counts consecutive invalid messages, answers pings, dispatches other valid messages, and contains handler failures. Parallel serving races it against device revalidation and connection closure.
blocks.title: Validated connection service

blocks.text: device_socket accepts the socket, loads protocol state, applies handshake rate limiting, creates and registers the authenticated connection, sends welcome, serves it, and removes it with disconnect notification in finally.
blocks.title: Endpoint lifecycle

gotchas: Protocol files are loaded only on first connection.
ConnectionClosed is treated as normal transport termination rather than an internal error.
how_it_works: Races receive, revalidation, and close tasks
purpose: This websocket endpoint performs the hello negotiation and device-credential authentication, validates subsequent client messages, answers pings, and hands valid messages to an installed handler. It also rechecks device activity, closes revoked or failed connections, and emits only fixed sanitized protocol errors.
summary: Authenticates, validates, rate-limits, and serves the device websocket protocol.

symbols.summary: Holds per-connection websocket timeouts and message/run limits that tests can replace.
Lazily imports the protocol validator from the first complete candidate directory.
Clears the loaded validator, client-type cache, and dynamic module entry.
Reads and caches the schema-declared client-to-server message types for a validator.
Defines the async message and disconnect callback seam for the run manager.
Extracts a lower-case UUID message id suitable for an error reference.
Reads one websocket frame and classifies disconnect, size, binary, and text cases.
Parses JSON text or returns a sentinel for invalid or overly nested JSON.
Validates one parsed client message and rejects non-client message types.
Sends one sanitized v1 error and closes a pre-authentication websocket.
Performs the first-frame hello exchange, version negotiation, and device authentication.
Runs the authenticated receive loop, validating messages, answering pings, and dispatching handlers.
Attempts to send an error and reports whether the connection remained usable.
Periodically checks device activity and reports revocation or database fault.
Races message reading, device revalidation, and connection closure, then closes on recheck failures.
Owns the websocket endpoint from accept through handshake, welcome, service, and cleanup.
